premises.text: The toy industry has seen little of the interactive, grow-with-the-child innovation the founders want; Cognitoys put learning technology inside an internet-connected toy
premises.evidence_span: internet-connected smart toys that learn and grow with a child

premises.text: Dino Cognitoys deliver ongoing witty, educational conversation and content (jokes, stories, scavenger hunts) rather than one-off Q&A
premises.evidence_span: engaging over the course of weeks and hopefully years, and not just one-off question-answer type engagements

premises.text: A parent panel shows engagement metrics and controls (e.g. bedtime, future custom messages), enabling subscription/content/feature upsell beyond one-time toy cycles
Retail at $99.99 with strong hardware margins, Kickstarter/retail distribution, and holiday full launch after beta units

value.text: Fun and educational toy experiences that keep kids laughing, asking questions, and learning over time
value.evidence_span: We're supposed to be fun and educational

causal_links.evidence_span: creating that sassiness, that wittiness, but also being educational
build a platform around the Dino
move into a full launch this holiday season

notes: Low toy innovation folded into connected grow-with-child product thesis rather than separate market-size premise (§4.1.4/6). Jokes/stories/hunts as content cascade of one toy (§4.1.7). Watson contest/Kickstarter/Time honors treated as traction/history and excluded. COGS roadmap kept as quantitative detail of retail offer (§4.1.3/8). Singleton D2/D3 retained as parent-platform and GTM modules. Anti-template: toy product, parent/subscription platform, and retail launch separately revisable.
